heading: A declarative input→output relation
text:
### A declarative input→output relation [LTSL.1.1]

A `.dstest` is a declarative relation between an **input timeline** and the
**outputs a program must produce** — not a script. The author places facts on a
timeline (data) and declares the expected outputs (data); the runtime owns all
execution. A test must not sequence engine operations: the surface has no `pump`,
no `advance`-as-command, and no ordered mutation list.

This is sound because the runtime derives every engine operation from the
timeline. Pump cadence is an input the engine records ([RFCS.22]), and two
inputs pumped together can produce a different output from the same two inputs
pumped apart, so the cadence is not left free: at each stamp the runtime asserts
that stamp's inputs in source order ([LTSL.3.3]) and then pumps to quiescence
([LTSL.3.4], [RTIM.14.5]). The cadence, and with it every output, is therefore a
function of the timeline alone, and an author has nothing to sequence.
